properties.description: Platinum single crystal surface with (1x2) reconstruction

nodes.name: Pt(hkl) electrode pretreatment and assembly
nodes.procedure: Following flame annealing in a hydrogen flame and cooling in a mild stream of Ar, the Pt(hkl) single crystal (0.283 cm²) was mounted into the disk position of an insertable ring disk electrode assembly (Pine Instruments). Subsequently, the electrode was transferred into a thermostated standard three compartment electrochemical cell and immersed into the Ar-purged/O2-purged electrolyte (Ar: Bay Gas (Research Purity); 0.1 M KOH: Aldrich Semiconductor Grade prepared with triply pyrodistilled water) under potentiostatic control at ≈0.1 V.

nodes.name: Pt(110)(1×2) reconstruction
nodes.procedure: The measurements on Pt(110) were carried out on the reconstructed surface with (1×2) geometry, prepared according to ref. 20.
nodes.source_text: The measurements on Pt(110) were carried out on the reconstructed surface with (1×2) geometry, prepared according to ref. 20, hereafter this surface is denoted as Pt(110) only.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt(111) exhibits three separate potential regions: Hupd (0 < E < 0.4 V), double layer (ca. 0.4 V < E < 0.6 V), and 'butterfly region' (0.6 < E < 0.9 V) representing discharge of OH⁻ to form OHad.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt(111) is the only surface which exhibits three separate potential regions: the hydrogen underpotential deposition region (Hupd, 0 < E < 0.4 V) is directly followed by the double layer region (ca. 0.4 V < E < 0.6 V) and then the so-called 'butterfly region' (0.6 < E < 0.9 V).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt(100) shows no true double-layer region, with Hupd overlapping with OHad formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a and 3a show that a true double-layer potential region does not exist on either Pt(100) (Fig. 2a) or on Pt(110) (Fig. 3a), and that the Hupd region overlaps with the OHad formation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt(110) shows no true double-layer region, with Hupd overlapping with OHad formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a and 3a show that a true double-layer potential region does not exist on either Pt(100) (Fig. 2a) or on Pt(110) (Fig. 3a), and that the Hupd region overlaps with the OHad formation.

nodes.characterization_summary: ORR activities increase (111) > (100) > (110)(1×2) with apparent activation energies 47 kJ mol⁻¹ (Pt(111)), 42 kJ mol⁻¹ (Pt(100)), 37 kJ mol⁻¹ (Pt(110)) at η = 0.35 V; peroxide formation decreases with temperature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: activities increasing in the sequence (111) > (100) > (110)(1×2). Very similar apparent activation energies (37–47 ± 5 kJ mol⁻¹, η = 0.35 V) were found on all three surfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: Tafel slopes decrease with increasing temperature: Pt(111) 86→57 mV/dec, Pt(100) 112→60 mV/dec, Pt(110)(1×2) 192→83 mV/dec.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Tafel slopes on all three single crystal surfaces decrease with increasing temperature... Values for Pt(111) and Pt(100) are between 86 and 57 mV decade⁻¹ and 112 and 60 mV decade⁻¹, respectively. On Pt(110), the slopes are slightly higher going from ca. 192 to 83 mV decade⁻¹.
